opportunities.title: Authors' Contingency Fund
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to all kinds of professional authors resident in the UK or British citizens (fiction writers, illustrators, literary translators, scriptwriters, poets, journalists and others) for whom author-related activities make up a substantial amount of their annual income and are their primary source of income. Not open to editors, copywriters, salaried journalists, or authors at the start of their careers. Membership of the Society of Authors not required. Previous recipients must wait four full calendar years before reapplying.
opportunities.summary: Small, short-term hardship grants to professional authors in financial difficulty (in moments of crisis), to help them return to normal working practice. Can be used to make up lost income, cover shortfalls, ease impact of illness, support sudden changes to homelife, or help with one-off expenses such as a new boiler or laptop.

opportunities.title: Authors' Foundation
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to writers who have been previously published or have a contract for their project with a commercial UK or Irish publisher. For book projects: commissioned by a commercial UK/Irish publisher, or have had at least one book published commercially by a UK/Irish publisher as sole author/translator with strong likelihood of next book being published. For script projects: previously had work professionally performed on stage, screen or radio in UK/Ireland, or currently under contract to write such a script. Must have a non-contributory contract. Hybrid/self-published books not eligible; editors not eligible; AI-generated works not accepted; previous recipients must wait four years before re-applying.
opportunities.summary: Grants to help develop a work-in-progress, covering research, travel or other general expenditure for fiction, non-fiction, poetry and script projects. Applicants are also automatically considered for specific named awards (Eric Ambler, Taner Baybars, John Brooks, Antonia Fraser, Arthur Welton, Great Britain Sasakawa Grant).

opportunities.title: K Blundell Trust
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be under the age of 40 on Sunday 1 March 2026, be British by birth and currently resident in the United Kingdom, and have a previous work of which they are the sole author published with a commercial UK publisher. Grants only for one work-in-progress. Hybrid/self-published books not eligible; editors not eligible; AI-generated works not accepted; previous recipients must wait four years before re-applying.
opportunities.summary: Work-in-progress grants for British authors under 40 whose work aims to increase social awareness. Accepts submissions for fiction, non-fiction, poetry and script projects. The fund has now closed and will re-open for applications in 2027.

opportunities.title: Society of Authors' Access Fund
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to all authors (anyone who creates work for publication, broadcast or performance) meeting SoA membership criteria. Membership not required. Open to UK and Irish residents and British and Irish citizens. Applicants may only apply for one grant per calendar year; preference given to those who have not received funds previously.
opportunities.summary: Small grants for travel, subsistence, childcare or access needs for events, residencies, and retreats. The fund is currently closed for applications and is expected to re-open for applications in 2027.

opportunities.title: Strachey Trust Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to all authors (as defined by SoA criteria for Full Membership, though membership is not required) who are UK resident or British citizens, working on a specific full-length literary project with a strong likelihood of publication. One application per calendar year; successful applicants must wait four years before re-applying.
opportunities.summary: Grants to enable authors to travel to a UK or Republic of Ireland archive or collection to research manuscript material for a specific full-length literary project which has a strong likelihood of publication. Can cover travel, accommodation, subsistence, childcare/carer support, companion travel, and access needs.
